sources.quote: CHOP paid its CEO a record $7.7 million in 2021, more than the hospital spent on charity care in three years
sources.searcher_note: Same comparison (one executive's pay vs the hospital's charity care) for a single hospital, CHOP, 2021 pay. Not the national 919-hospital count.

sources.outlet: Massachusetts Nurses Association (citing Payers and Providers survey)
sources.quote: The survey also identified 17 hospitals in California where the total compensation to CEOs exceeded the cost of charity care.
sources.searcher_note: Earliest found: same measure (CEO pay above charity-care cost), California only, 17 of 118 nonprofit hospitals, 2009 pay data. Different place and window.

sources.outlet: U.S. Senate HELP Committee Majority Staff (Sanders)
sources.quote: just over half of the hospitals reviewed by HELP Committee staff provided their CEO with a 2021 salary that was more than 6 percent of their total outlay for charity care.
sources.searcher_note: 16 largest nonprofit systems, 2021: CEO pay as a share of charity care (highest Allina at 21%). System level, not hospital level; none reported above 100%.

sources.quote: A one million dollar increase in charity care had no significant association with CEO compensation.
sources.searcher_note: Form 990 study of nonprofit hospital CEO pay 2012 and 2019: pay tracks profits, not charity care. Pattern, no count of hospitals where pay exceeds charity care.

sources.quote: This restrictive approach not only departs from the relevant regulatory framework but also overlooks the vital role
sources.searcher_note: Disagreement on framing: AHA argues judging hospitals on charity care alone is too narrow (excludes Medicaid shortfall, other community benefit). Does not address officer pay.

sources.quote: excessive executive compensation more befitting Fortune 500 companies
sources.searcher_note: Post-cutoff: roundup of support for nonprofit hospital transparency push; mentions executive pay criticism but no direct pay-vs-charity-care comparison or count.

notes: No source found giving a national count or share of nonprofit hospitals where one officer's 2022 pay exceeded the hospital's charity-care cost. Same measure appears for single hospitals (CHOP 2021, Philadelphia Inquirer) and for California 2009 (17 of 118 hospitals, about 14%). Senate HELP 2023 covers 16 big systems at system level. Also found: Save Our States report covered by yournews.com 2026-06-29 (NewYork-Presbyterian CEO pay vs under 1% of revenue to charity care), not recorded to stay within 6. NPR 2024-08-19 piece on CEO pay vs community benefit timed out on fetch twice, not recorded. Axios Cleveland 2023 (Cleveland Clinic 1.5% charity care, CEO $6.6M) seen in search results, not fetched.
